opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research max £20,000; Research and Travel max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply under the Research and Travel category. Individuals independently wishing to develop their own practice are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and fund research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, and development of collections through acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing and display. Applications are considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire for the duration of the fellowship

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture. Research Fellowships at the Institute are for academics or curators; Artist Research Fellowships for artists; Senior Fellowships (six weeks) for established scholars. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens are for researchers whose interests lie in Henry Moore specifically.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships allow researchers to spend a month using the Foundation's facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 cash prize for MA dissertation; winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines who submitted a dissertation within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Henry Moore Institute awards two prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. Submissions should have a strong focus on secondary and primary sources and original research. The 2026 prize submissions will open in autumn.
